article_title: To compare PubMed Clinical Queries and UpToDate in teaching information mastery to clinical residents: a crossover randomized controlled trial.
citation: Sayyah Ensan Ladan, Faghankhani Masoomeh, Javanbakht Anna, Ahmadi Seyed-Foad, Baradaran Hamid Reza. (2011). To Compare PubMed Clinical Queries and UpToDate in Teaching Information Mastery to Clinical Residents: A Crossover Randomized Controlled Trial. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0023487
title: The 5S/6S hierarchy of evidence-based information resources
description: The article teaches and applies the 5S model of information resources, in which evidence is arranged as "systems, summaries, synopses, syntheses and studies arranged through the highest to the lowest level resources, respectively", recently extended to a 6S model adding synopses of syntheses. Both models "suggest looking for the needed information at the highest level and proceeding to lower levels in case of failure to find the relevant evidence". The workshop lecture introduced the 5S or 6S pyramid and how to use it, and the study operationalizes the contrast between a higher-level summary source (UpToDate) and a lower-level raw database (PubMed Clinical Queries).
requirements: Learners must be taught the pyramid and how to search within higher-level resources before lower ones
constraints: The article notes computerized decision support systems (the systems level) are not well developed yet
target_learners: postgraduate year-one or two medical residents
target_learning_goals: information mastery: finding the best evidence in a short time
examples: The one-hour workshop lecture included an introduction of the 5S or 6S pyramid and how to use it, and classification of 20 resources into predigested and raw databases
